newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sustained growth at CEPA seen difficult.
newsitem.headline: Sustained growth at CEPA seen difficult.

text.p: New projects are expected to double Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) income but the company may have difficulty sustaining steady growth in the years ahead, analysts said.

Gordon Wu, chairman of CEPA and managing director of its parent Hopewell Holdings Ltd, told local newspapers that new projects coming on line would double CEPA's income over the next couple of months, but analysts were not impressed.
"This is nothing new as the market already expected the completion of the Shajiao C and Pagbilao power plants to lift CEPA earnings greatly," an analyst at a European house said.
Shajiao C Power Station in China's Guangdong province and Philippines Pagbilao Power Station started operations recently.
CEPA has a 32 percent interest in Shajiao C, which has total capacity of 1,980 mw, and 86.95 percent in Pagbilao, which has two 367.5 mw generators.
"This will boost CEPA's 1996/97 earnings to more than double," a research analyst at a Japanese brokerage said.
But analysts said they were concerned about steady profit growth in the following years.
"CEPA will probably have to wait until the turn of the century for more new projects to come on stream," the Japanese house analyst said.

Analysts expected the power operator to post net profit of between HK$1.1 billion and HK$1.8 billion in the year to June 30, 1997, up from the HK$589 million to HK$625 million expected for the year ended last June 30.
CEPA had 1994/95 net profit of HK$565 million.
Earnings from power generation was expected to rise to more than 70 percent of total earnings this fiscal year from 30 percent in 1995/96, an analyst with an American house said.
Sual Power Station in the Philippines, with two 660 mw generators, is expected to be completed by June 1999 and would be the earliest project under construction to be completed.
Analysts said CEPA shares were overvalued following a recent surge which was fuelled by speculation Hopewell would sell a stake in its unit.
"The price of CEPA shares had been lifted by rumours that an American power operator offered HK$18 a share for Hopewell's CEPA shares," a broker said.
Shares of CEPA slipped 15 cents to close at HK$16.35 on Monday while the Hang Seng index surged 143.04 points to 11,902.43.
Hopewell has said it was talking to several overseas investors who were interested in buying part of or all of its 60.4 percent stake in CEPA.
Wu told local reporters this weekend he hoped to maintain management of CEPA after the possible sale.
"Hopewell probably would need to retain more than 30 percent in CEPA in order to secure an effective control," the American house analyst said.
